source_text: Si Deus homines creat, non possunt cum aliquo malo nasci. Si nuptiae bonum sunt, nihil ex eis oritur mali. Si in Baptismate peccata omnia remittuntur, non possunt nati de renatis trahere originale peccatum. Si iustus est Deus, non potest in filiis parentum damnare peccata, cum ipsis parentibus dimittat et propria. Si perfectae iustitiae capax est humana natura, habere non potest vitia naturalia
pass_a_gloss: If God human-beings creat, not are-able when/with aliquo to-evil to-be-born. if marriages good are, nothing from to-them arises of-evil. if in in-baptism sins all-things remittuntur, not are-able born about/from from-the-reborn trahere original sin. if just is God, not is-able in filiis of-parents damnare sins, when/with ipsis parents dimittat and own. if of-perfect of-justice capable is humana nature, to-have not is-able faults natural.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: If God creates human beings, they cannot be born with any evil. If marriage is good, no evil comes from it. If all sins are forgiven in baptism, those born from people who have been born again cannot inherit original sin. If God is just, he cannot condemn parents’ sins in their children when he forgives the parents their own sins. If human nature is capable of perfect righteousness, it cannot have natural faults.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
